title: How do I get Cilium to run on WSL2?
body: My Cilium pods crash on 1.15.0-pre.2 with: `failed while reinitializing datapath: removing ipv6 proxy routing rule: address family not supported by protocol`. Version 1.14.4 works fine. This is a kind cluster on WSL2 with Kubernetes 1.28.3 and a custom-compiled linux-msft-wsl-5.15.133.1 kernel configured by following Cilium's system requirements. I suspect this may be related to IPv6, but I do not know what changed between 1.14.4 and 1.15.0-pre.2.

symptoms_visible: My Cilium 1.15.0-pre.2 pods crash with `removing ipv6 proxy routing rule: address family not supported by protocol`, while 1.14.4 works on the same WSL2 kind environment.
N0.label: N0 Cilium 1.15 startup failure reported

symptoms_visible: Cilium 1.15.0-pre.2 still exits while removing the IPv6 proxy routing rule.
N1.label: N1 custom kernel configuration inspected

symptoms_visible: I installed Cilium with `ipv6.enabled=false`, but it still exits with the same `address family not supported by protocol` error.
N1_x.label: N1_x disabling Cilium IPv6 aftermath

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with `CONFIG_IPV6_SEG6_LWTUNNEL=y`, the original proxy-rule error is gone, but Cilium still stops with `NewHandleAt failed: protocol not supported` from `*linux.devicesController.Start`.
N2_x.label: N2_x single IPv6 kernel option aftermath

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding and selecting a WSL2 kernel with the required networking options and modules, Cilium starts and runs without either protocol-support startup error.
N_terminal.label: terminal Cilium running on rebuilt WSL2 kernel

question_patterns: What value does `CONFIG_IPV6_MULTIPLE_TABLES` have in your config-wsl file?
Could you check whether `CONFIG_IPV6_MULTIPLE_TABLES` is set in the kernel config you compiled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked the config-wsl file, and `CONFIG_IPV6_MULTIPLE_TABLES` is not set.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I checked the active kernel config and all of the relevant routing-table and protocol-family entries are enabled with the documented values.
The entry is unset in config-wsl, but I am using a slightly newer build of the same WSL2 kernel series.

question_patterns: Does the kernel have IPv6 disabled entirely, or is `CONFIG_IPV6=y` present?
What IPv6-related entries are enabled in the config-wsl file?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is not disabled entirely: `CONFIG_IPV6=y`, and some IPv6 modules are enabled in the config. I am far from an expert on Linux kernel compilation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The base protocol support is disabled in my active kernel config.

edges.comment: Issue c1, c4 and c5 on the opening reporter's WSL2 system: participant1 prompted inspection of the kernel config, and the reporter confirmed that multiple routing tables were unset even though base IPv6 support was enabled.

solution.intent: Treat the kernel as lacking usable IPv6 and disable Cilium IPv6 during installation.
solution.concrete_example: Reinstall or upgrade Cilium with `--set ipv6.enabled=false` and retry startup.

edges.comment: Issue c2 and c7-c8 on the opening reporter's system: disabling Cilium IPv6 was suggested for a kernel without usable v6 support, but the reporter explicitly installed with the flag and observed the same startup error.

solution.intent: Enable only the IPv6 segment-routing lightweight-tunnel kernel option, rebuild the WSL2 kernel, and retry Cilium.
solution.concrete_example: Set `CONFIG_IPV6_SEG6_LWTUNNEL=y`, rebuild and boot the custom WSL2 kernel, then start Cilium again.

edges.comment: Issue c2 and c9 on the opening reporter's system: the reporter enabled CONFIG_IPV6_SEG6_LWTUNNEL after learning it pulls in related support. This removed the original error but left Cilium failing at the devices controller with a new raw `protocol not supported` error, so the single-option change was incomplete.

solution.intent: Use a WSL2 kernel with the complete Cilium-required networking configuration, including the missing IPv6 routing capabilities; build and install its modules, select that kernel through .wslconfig, restart WSL2, load the modules, and verify Cilium starts.
solution.concrete_example: Start from a clean WSL2 kernel source/config, enable the Cilium-documented networking, XFRM, tunnel and IPv6 options—including `CONFIG_IPV6_MULTIPLE_TABLES`—then build the kernel and loadable modules, run `modules_install`, copy the bzImage to Windows, point `%USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig` at it, run `wsl --shutdown`, and load the documented modules. Confirm `uname -r` shows the intended kernel and that the Cilium agents remain running.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw config values and successive startup errors. Maintainers explained that older Cilium setup scripts used `ip rule ... || true`, while the newer implementation no longer hid these errors. Combining the unset routing-table entry with the second protocol error after enabling one related feature establishes that the custom WSL2 kernel had an incomplete feature set, rather than IPv6 simply being disabled in Cilium.

edges.comment: Issue c10, c17 and c20 on the opening reporter's own WSL2 system: the reporter confirmed Cilium worked after enabling the required networking options, later documented building/installing the kernel and modules and selecting it via .wslconfig, and clarified that a WSL2 kernel containing IPv6 multiple-routing-table support works with Cilium's documented option set. Comments c21-c30 concern participant3's separate WSL2 deployment and are not spliced into the opening reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the custom WSL2 kernel had an incomplete IPv6/networking configuration, notably missing IPv6 multiple-routing-table support and related capabilities, even though `CONFIG_IPV6=y` was enabled.

Must explain the version difference using the thread's evidence: newer Cilium code exposed netlink or routing-rule errors that older shell commands had suppressed, revealing the deficient kernel configuration.
The recommendation must use or rebuild a WSL2 kernel with the complete Cilium-documented networking options, install and load its modules, and ensure WSL2 actually boots that kernel.
Must not present `ipv6.enabled=false` as the fix; the reporter tried it and received the same startup error.
Must not present enabling only the segment-routing lightweight-tunnel option as sufficient; it removed the first error but Cilium then failed with another `protocol not supported` error.
Must ask the user to confirm the intended kernel with `uname -r` and verify that Cilium starts and remains running before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: A technically capable Kubernetes developer who can follow build instructions and compile a custom WSL2 kernel, but explicitly describes themselves as new to Linux kernel compilation and open-source contribution.
persona_hint.communication_style: Friendly, candid and cooperative; shares exact errors and configuration findings, tests suggestions quickly, uses humor and emoji when describing unfamiliar kernel work, and later writes detailed reproducible instructions.
